chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Awrama, from Al-Nadr, from Yahya ibn Abi Khalid Al-Qammat, from Humran ibn A'yan, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you! How few we are — if we were to gather together upon a sheep, we would not (even be able to) finish it.' So he said: 'Shall I narrate to you something more strange than that? The Emigrants and the Helpers were gone,' — and he gestured with his hand — 'except three.'

Humran said: 'So I said: "May I be sacrificed for you! What is the state of Ammar?" He said: "May Allah have mercy on Ammar — Abu al-Yaqzan — he pledged allegiance and was killed as a martyr." So I said within myself: "What thing is more superior than martyrdom?" So he looked at me and said: "Perhaps you think he is like the three. Far be it! Far be it!"

key_terms.أَبَا الْيَقْظَانِ: Abu al-Yaqzan ('the Alert/Wakeful') — the kunya (agnomen) of Ammar ibn Yasir
key_terms.أَيْهَاتَ: far be it — an expression of emphatic negation and impossibility, denying any equivalence
key_terms.الثَّلَاثَةِ: the three — Salman al-Farsi, Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, and Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, who alone among the Emigrants and Helpers maintained unwavering allegiance to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْأَنْصَارُ: the Helpers — the people of Medina who aided the Prophet (SAWW) and the Emigrants
key_terms.الْمُهَاجِرُونَ: the Emigrants — the companions who migrated with the Prophet (SAWW) from Mecca to Medina
key_terms.بَايَعَ: pledged allegiance — gave bay'ah, here referring to Ammar's pledge after the passing of the Prophet (SAWW)
key_terms.شَهِيداً: as a martyr — one who is killed in the path of God, a rank of high honour

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir (AS) say about the rank of Ammar ibn Yasir compared to Salman, Abu Dharr, and Miqdad?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) responds to Humran ibn A'yan's remark about the small number of true believers by pointing to a still more astonishing reality: nearly all the Emigrants and Helpers abandoned the true path after the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), save for only three — Salman, Abu Dharr, and Miqdad. When Humran asks about Ammar ibn Yasir's standing, the Imam affirms Ammar's martyrdom with supplication for his mercy, yet — perceiving Humran's unspoken assumption — emphatically declares that Ammar's rank is not equivalent to those three steadfast companions, underscoring the supreme spiritual station of unwavering allegiance.
